records.title: Comparative functional analysis of DPYD variants of potential clinical relevance to dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase activity
records.role: Functional study CPIC cites for c.557A>G (p.Y186C). Independent of CPIC.
abstract_excerpts: Enzyme activity was also significantly reduced for 30 additional variants, 19 of which had <25% activity.
None of those 30 variants have been previously reported to associate with 5-FU toxicity in clinical association studies, which have been conducted primarily in populations of European ancestry.
Using publicly available genotype databases, we confirmed the rarity of these variants in European populations but showed that they are detected at appreciable frequencies in other populations.
records.limitation_recorded: Its discussion reports the Y186C substitution reduced activity by approximately 15% relative to wild type, 'less than we expected', and notes a prior study focused on this variant found a similar reduction. CPIC's Decreased function / 0.5 assignment is therefore a curation judgement over several lines of evidence, not a restatement of this single effect size.

records.title: Prevalence of the DPYD variant (Y186C) in Brazilian individuals of African ancestry
records.role: Independent population-frequency source for the African-ancestry relevance.
abstract_excerpts: The variant Y186C (rs115232898) is found almost exclusively in African populations and is related to low DPD function.

The variant Y186C was found in heterozygosity in two samples from Southeast (2.53%) and one from Northeast (2.77%) Brazil. Overall, the prevalence of this mutation in the 115 African Brazilians was 2.6%.
should be taken in account in targeted genotyping for fluoropyrimidine risk variants
